work.description: Orchestrate iterative implementation work from GitHub issues by default, or from a prompt file when you pass its path: classify each objective, delegate test-writer → implementer → reviewer to fresh sub-agents while the main session stays a pure orchestrator, execute each approved objective's see-it-work probe against the real target before it closes, surface ambiguities as decisions, hold against spec drift, then queue what remains. Issues carrying the selector label (--label, default pb-backlog) are worked milestone by milestone (due date, then milestone number), in priority order inside each (priority:p0 through priority:p3, oldest first within a band), claimed with pb-in-progress while in flight, and closed on completion, so the same backlog is workable from any machine. Small backlog items bundle into one run by default (cap 3), each running its own full chain in sequence; pass --single for one objective, or --batch N to change the cap. Each phase routes independently to a native sub-agent or a chosen harness and model (backend@model over pi, claude, or opencode; defaulted per phase by an optional .pb/delegates roster), and offloaded workers are hosted in herdr panes when the session runs under herdr. Pass --stack to freeze each phase as a commit on its own gh-stack branch (slug optional; derived from the objective when omitted), or --commit to commit the approved work in place on the current branch. Pass --auto to answer every mid-run question with the durable default (best forward-facing architectural choice; never descope, waive a probe, or commit unreviewed) so the run never waits on you. Pre-deployment by default; pass --prod to treat the code as live. Use when asked to work the issues, work the backlog, work the prompt, or run prompt.md.
